themes_detail.label: Illegal Postings Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Illegal postings complaints spiked to 6 this week versus a baseline of 0.4 per week—a 1500% increase—suggesting a coordinated or sudden campaign of unlicensed advertising across Queens Village/Cambria Heights.
evidence: 6 illegal posting complaints this week vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 11.62)
Highest statistical anomaly in dataset by z-score, indicating sudden departure from baseline
Previous week reported 6 complaints as well, suggesting sustained spike
reporting_angles: Ground truth: Walk the neighborhood to identify where illegal postings are concentrated and what they're advertising
Interview 311 operations or NYPD about whether this is linked to a known advertising network or event

themes_detail.label: Curb Damage & Street Signs Vanishing
themes_detail.summary: This week, curb condition complaints jumped 833% (14 this week vs. 1.5 weekly average) and missing street signs jumped 586% (6 this week vs. 0.9 weekly average), suggesting either deliberate damage, infrastructure neglect, or a single incident affecting multiple blocks.
evidence: Curb condition: 14 complaints this week vs. 1.5 weekly average (z-score: 7.91)
Street sign missing: 6 complaints this week vs. 0.9 weekly average (z-score: 5.53)
Two infrastructure categories spiking simultaneously suggests common cause (weather event, construction, or vandalism)
reporting_angles: Check DOT records for active street work or recent construction that may explain curb and sign damage
Map the 311 complaints geographically to see if damage is clustered on specific streets (possible targeted incident)

themes_detail.label: Tree Overgrowth Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Overgrown tree and branch complaints jumped 383% this week (35 complaints vs. 7.2 weekly average), the highest-volume spike in the dataset, indicating widespread hazardous vegetation that may block sidewalks, roads, or utilities.
evidence: 35 overgrown tree/branch complaints this week vs. 7.2 weekly average (z-score: 5.5)
Largest complaint volume spike in dataset in absolute terms
Aligns with community board recurring request for better park maintenance and street tree management
reporting_angles: Interview residents about which blocks have the worst overgrowth and what safety hazards it's creating (blocked sidewalks, obscured traffic signals, downed lines)
Ask Parks Dept why this spike is happening now and when they can address backlog—link to chronic underfunding reflected in CB budget requests

themes_detail.label: Vehicle Noise Surge
themes_detail.summary: Vehicle noise complaints jumped 300% this week (12 complaints vs. 3.0 weekly average), suggesting either a spike in illegal drag racing, modified exhaust vehicles, or construction activity that residents are reporting at elevated rates.
evidence: 12 vehicle noise complaints this week vs. 3.0 weekly average (z-score: 4.99)
Complements broader noise category (residential noise at 599 complaints over 90 days, suggesting ongoing quality-of-life issue)
Suggests concentrated problem this week, not long-running trend
reporting_angles: Speak with residents and NYPD about whether this is tied to known drag racing corridors or a one-time event
Check social media or NextDoor posts for community complaints about specific times/locations to pinpoint source

themes_detail.label: Air Quality & Rodent Spike
themes_detail.summary: Air quality complaints jumped 380% this week (6 vs. 1.2 weekly average) and rodent complaints jumped 336% (6 vs. 1.4 weekly average), both environmental health concerns that may signal a broader sanitation or pollution issue in the district.
evidence: Air quality: 6 complaints this week vs. 1.2 weekly average (z-score: 4.91)
Rodent: 6 complaints this week vs. 1.4 weekly average (z-score: 4.66)
Two environmental health spikes in same week suggest possible common source (illegal dumping, backed-up sewer, uncollected waste)
reporting_angles: Investigate whether recent construction permits (656 total filed in past 90 days) or demolition activity (16 full demolitions) have created dust or contamination
Check DEP and DSNY records for recent sanitation complaints, illegal dumping reports, or water main breaks in the area
